representative_tasks.task: Interpret p = 0.03 from an A/B test
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: States the conditional definition (data at least this extreme if H0 and assumptions hold), not the probability H0 is true, and asks for the effect size and CI

representative_tasks.task: Decide whether a t-test on mean latency is valid for heavy-tailed data
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Names the finite-variance condition of the CLT and recommends estimand-appropriate robust methods

representative_tasks.task: Test whether model A beats model B from cross-validation scores
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Rejects the naive fold-wise paired t-test and recommends a corrected resampled t-test or 5x2cv, or on a held-out test set a paired bootstrap or DeLong's test for the AUC difference (McNemar only for thresholded accuracy)

negative_cases: Misconception that a tiny Mann-Whitney p-value shows the new variant raises average revenue (planned)
Peeking: stopping an A/B test the first day p < 0.05 appears (planned)
rubric: States the assumptions a test or theorem needs (finite variance, independence) and checks them against the scenario
Separates statistical significance from effect size and practical relevance
Recommends a named procedure suited to the data and estimand rather than a generic 'use a non-parametric test'
Does not endorse an invalid p-value
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
The cases do not recompute any statistic a response reports; a wrong corrected p-value would not be caught by hard assertions.

Paraphrase robustness was spot-checked once with 4 answers written by the pattern author after the patterns were set (one correct and one wrong per case): before any fix, 1/2 correct answers passed and 2/2 wrong answers failed. Misses were fixed by broadening patterns and all 4 answers were kept as .probe fixtures, so they are no longer held out and the probe was not blind.

Independent probe (Phase 2 review): 7 answers for this skill's cases written by a reviewer who did not write the patterns, graded once before any change. Before the fix 3/3 correct answers passed and only 1/4 plausible on-topic wrong answers failed (31 answers across the five skills of this workstream: 11/14 correct passed, 5/16 wrong failed). Most misses were hedge-word escape hatches ('only', 'not', 'if') that fired on the wrong answer's own wording, and concept patterns satisfied by negated mentions. The patterns were then fixed and the reviewer's answers kept verbatim as .pass.blind* / .fail.adversarial* fixtures, so they now grade as expected only because the patterns were tuned to them and are no longer held out.

Fix-engineer probe: 4 further answers (.pass.fixprobe / .fail.fixprobe) written by the engineer who then edited the patterns, after reading the review but before editing, graded once: 2/2 correct passed and 2/2 wrong failed before the fix (8/10 and 8/10 across the five skills). This is author-adjacent, not blind, and the answers are now fixtures. Expect real model outputs to find further phrasings that neither probe anticipated; the rubric remains authoritative.
unsupported_use_cases: Choosing model performance metrics such as AUC, F1 or calibration (model-evaluation)
